column1: engineering-manager-core-team-hamburg-409647,Metergrid,Engineering Manager (m/w/d) – Core Team,Hamburg,False,1791608976,"Deine AufgabenWir bauen die Software, mit der Mieterstromprojekte laufen: Zählerdaten rein, Abrechnung raus, und alles dazwischen. Das Core Team verantwortet das Betreiberportal, das Produkt, auf dem der laufende Betrieb unserer Kunden steht. Es ist unser fachlich tiefstes Team, und es wächst.Das Betreiberportal ist kein generisches SaaS. Es bildet die Energiewirtschaft ab: Messstellenbetrieb, Marktkommunikation, Netzentgelte, Umlagen, Abrechnung nach Regeln, die der Gesetzgeber schreibt und regelmäßig ändert. Wer hier priorisiert, muss verstehen, was eine Anforderung für den Betreiber wirtschaftlich bedeutet und was passiert, wenn sie falsch umgesetzt wird.Dafür suchen wir eine Person, die das Team führt und das Geschäft dahinter versteht. Nicht als Durchreiche für Tickets und nicht als Architekt, der alles selbst entscheidet, sondern als jemand, der Business-Anforderungen in technische Entscheidungen übersetzt und dafür sorgt, dass gute Entwickler gute Arbeit machen können: klare Ziele, wenig Reibung, ehrliches Feedback, verlässliche Lieferung.Der Weg dahin ist bewusst gewählt: Du startest für rund sechs Monate als Entwickler im Core Team. Du baust Features, machst Reviews und lernst Codebasis, Fachlichkeit und Menschen von innen kennen. Danach übernimmst du die Führung des Teams. Wer ein Team führen will, das er nie von innen gesehen hat, führt es an dem vorbei, was zählt.Technisch: Python mit Django und Django Ninja im Backend, React mit TypeScript im Frontend, PostgreSQL mit TimescaleDB, deployt auf Kubernetes per GitOps mit ArgoCD. KI-Coding-Assistenten sind fester Teil des Workflows. In den ersten Monaten schreibst du diesen Code selbst. Danach musst du ihn weiter lesen können und verstehen, worüber dein Team diskutiert.In den ersten sechs MonatenDu arbeitest als Entwickler im Core Team: Features end-to-end, Reviews, Deployments, Support-Fälle. column1: account-executive-full-cycle-new-business-berlin-431496,Mute Labs Gmbh,"Account Executive – Full-Cycle, New Business (m/f/d)",Berlin,False,1791598148,"THE JOBReading this to the end is worth it.The Company: Why mute-labs?mute-labs is the EU market leader in acoustic phone booths, with more than 20,000 cabins sold and counting. We are self-funded, profitable since day one, and have no investors to answer to and no exit to chase. What we do have is a steep growth curve in revenue, a product made in Germany, and a genuine mission: giving the modern office some quiet back.We have built a strong direct and dealer business on the back of inbound demand and word of mouth. What we have not built yet is a real outbound engine for winning bigger accounts on purpose, from ambitious growth companies to household names like Volkswagen, adidas, IKEA, Red Bull, or Axel Springer, who already trust us today. That gap is this role, and how far into that world you grow is largely up to you.Outbound is not a new idea for us. We have piloted it in smaller pockets already, testing signal-based outreach and structured sequences with real results. What has been missing is someone to own this as a dedicated motion for bigger accounts rather than a side project squeezed in between other things. That is why we are building this out as a new department and you’d be joining a small, yet focussed team as one of the first hires.The Role: Build the Pipeline AND the ChannelThis is a founding position. You are not stepping into an existing sales org with a quota handed down from three reps before you. You are the first one in the building. What you build, and how you build it, is largely up to you and your team, and you can grow the size and ambition of your target accounts as you find your footing.Green Field, Full Ownership: Build your own pipeline from scratch. There is no inherited book of business and no recycled leads. The customer base you build is yours, and so is the revenue you generate from it.Your Stack, Your Sequences: Clay, Reply.io, LinkedIn Premium, and Aircall are all at your disposal. You design your own outreach sequences, run your own cold calling campaigns, and decide how the machine works. Nobody hands you a script.Segment Strategy, Together: You understand the market as well as anyone. Rather than being handed a target list from above, you and your manager will decide together which segments and account types are worth focusing on.Comp That Rewards More Than the First Deal: An uncapped bonus with a kicker for overperformance. Returning customers you bring in keep feeding your comp over time, not just the initial close. Landing an account well is worth more than landing it once.A Brand That Opens Doors: You are not cold-calling on behalf of an unknown startup. mute-labs is an established, well-regarded market leader with a reference list that already includes some of the biggest names in German and European business. That credibility is yours to use from day one.A seasoned team to back you up: Your manager has built and run outbound and enterprise sales hands-on, from cold pipeline to six-figure closes, and will work closely with you from day one, coaching, supporting, and training wherever it's actually needed rather than just checking in on numbers.Is This You?The Go-Getter: You do not wait to be told what to do next. You get on your feet quickly, figure out the shape of the problem, and start moving before anyone has to push you.Sales Experience: You have carried a full sales cycle before, from first contact to signed contract, and know how to keep a deal moving without needing someone else to close it for you. You do not need to have sold into large enterprises already, that is something you will grow into here.Stakeholder Management: You know how to work a deal with more than one person in the room, decision-makers, influencers, and budget holders, and you can keep several of those relationships moving in parallel without losing the thread.Comfortable with Ambiguity: There is no existing playbook to inherit here. You will help write it. If you need every process defined for you before you can start, this is not the role.Fluent in German and English: Most of your target accounts are DACH-based, though the reference list extends across the EU. Strong German is expected

C'est une page blanche côté growth, et c'est exactement ce qui rend le poste intéressant. On cherche quelqu'un pour construire, mesurer et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition de l'Academy à partir de zéro : quels canaux, quels messages, quel funnel, avec quels résultats. Pas pour décorer le catalogue, pour le remplir.
1. Construire et faire tourner le moteur d'acquisition, avec le Head of Marketing &amp
Structurer le tunnel d'acquisition de bout en bout : quels canaux amènent du trafic, ce qui convertit en lead, ce qui déclenche l'inscription
Tester des canaux et des formats en continu (LinkedIn organique et payant, email, SEO, partenariats, salons) et couper vite ce qui ne marche pas
Créer et itérer les landing pages du catalogue et des sessions, pensées pour convertir dès le premier jet et retravaillées à partir de la donnée
Mettre en place les séquences email dans HubSpot : nurturing, relances, réactivation des contacts dormants, avec un test A/B sur les objets et les CTA
Accompagner le lancement des nouvelles formations avec un plan d'acquisition dédié, pas seulement un plan de com
Créer les supports nécessaires au tunnel avec Figma (catalogue, plaquettes, brochures) en gardant en tête qu'un support existe pour convertir, pas pour exister
Représenter l'Academy sur des salons et événements, avec un objectif de leads qualifiés en sortie, pas juste de présence
Le nerf du poste. Sans mesure, pas de growth, juste du marketing qui se raconte des histoires.

column1: senior-industrial-designer-robotics-berlin-223822,Cell Labs,Senior Industrial Designer | Robotics,Berlin,False,1791576575,"Your tasksShape the hardware identity: Define how our humanoids look and feel: proportions, surfaces, overall silhouette. You work through clearances, pinch points, contact surfaces and fall behavior so the robot is safe around people before software gets involved.Integrate complex systems: Package the internals (sensors, cameras, cooling, connectors, cable routing) so the technical parts look intended.Physical human machine interaction: Design status signals, touchpoints and small physical cues that tell the people working next to the robot what it is doing and what comes next.Build the ecosystem around the robot: Extend the design language to charging docks, transport cases, maintenance gear and packaging.From model to CAD: You build physical models fast, see what holds up, and change them until they do. Then you do the surfacing and hand over CAD that engineering can build from directly.Materials and processes: Select finishes, review physical samples, and work suppliers on feasibility, cost and lead times. You are willing to try materials that are not standard and to bring in specialized external labs.Your profileBackground: A degree in industrial or product design, or an engineering degree where the design side is clearly the stronger half.Experience: Around five years or more designing physical products, in house or at a studio. Robotics, medical devices, lab and industrial equipment, mobility, or another field where the hardware has to hold up in front of people.Small series: You have worked on products built in the hundreds rather than the millions, and know how much that changes what a shape can be.Safety and regulation: You have designed under mechanical safety requirements before, so guarding, clearances and contact safety are familiar territory rather than a new topic.Tools: Surface modeling in Rhino, Onshape, SolidWorks or Fusion, plus 3D printing and enough workshop practice to build your own models.Working with engineers: You read mechanical drawings, keep up in technical discussions, and can explain why a design decision matters.Languages: Fluent English. column1: remote-senior-sales-manager-uk-hamburg-237114,Moebel De,Senior Sales Manager UK,Hamburg,True,1791576546,"Our project for you:moebel.de is Europe's leading price comparison site for furniture and home furnishings. The launch is done, the technology works. What decides the pace now are the retailers: the more relevant shops list their ranges on living24.uk, the stronger the comparison for users – and the faster the portal grows.This is not selling from a tidy list of existing accounts. You take on a freshly launched market and build the partner portfolio that living24.uk runs on. Whoever delivers over the next few months will shape what moebel.de looks like in the UK.That is why we are looking for you as Senior Sales Manager UK.Your future TasksBuilding the market: you build living24.uk's partner portfolio – from first contact through pitch and negotiation to the signed contract. Your targets are UK online retailers in furniture, home furnishings, garden, décor, white goods, home electronics and small appliances.Selling a performance model: you show retailers how living24.uk pays off as an additional channel – through cost per click, visibility, feed quality and cost-of-sale.Seeing partners through to go-live: product feed, tracking, range checks – together with the team in Hamburg. After go-live our Relationship Management team takes over day-to-day care, so you can focus on winning new partners.Presence in the market: retailer visits, trade fairs and industry events across the UK. In a young market, trust is built face to face.Ear to the ground: competition, price levels, what UK retailers expect, seasonality – what you learn in the field feeds into product, pricing and priorities.Your StrenghtsSeveral years of sales experience in UK e-commerce, ideally with a price comparison site, marketplace, affiliate network or performance marketing providerA solid network of UK retailers in our categories that you can put to work from day oneCommand of the performance model: CPC, CPO, affiliate, product feeds, ROAS and cost-of-sale are selling points for you, not buzzwordsA hunter's mindset: you keep your own pipeline full, cold outreach included, and get deals over the lineAn appetite for building: pace and open questions appeal to you more than a field that has already been ploughedWorking from the numbers, with clean CRM records as the basis for how you steerWillingness to travel across the UK and to regular meetings in HamburgFluent English at negotiation level – German is a plus, not a requirementOur BenefitsYour day is yours to shapeWork when you are most productive. Early bird or night owl: you set your hours flexibly, in agreement with your team. Working from another European country for a while? No problem. Your laptop is your workplace.Our culture is one of a kindHere everyone sits on the same couch, regardless of title or role. We live team spirit online and in person – gaming nights, workouts, film evenings and team events.Four times a year we meet for Company WeekWorking together in the office, pushing projects forward, pizza evenings and a party to finish.In the heart of HamburgWhen you are in Hamburg, our office is waiting for you – centrally located between the main station, Mönckebergstraße and the Binnenalster lake. Perfect for lunch dates, a break by the Alster or a stroll after work.We are looking forward to receiving your application!Please send your application exclusively through our online application form – it goes straight to our recruiting team. column1: head-of-finance-berlin-397449,Superchat,Head of Finance (m/f/d),Berlin,False,1791607967,"At Superchat, we're rebuilding how businesses talk to their customers. Founded in 2020, Superchat has become the platform of choice for 10,000+ businesses worldwide, from globally recognized brands like Allianz, Auto1, Enpal, Danone, and GASAG to the small businesses, dental practices, and one-person startups that need to look bigger than they are. Today, millions of messages flow through Superchat every single day.

We started as a unified inbox: one place for every channel a customer might pick, WhatsApp, email, SMS, Instagram. Then ChatGPT happened, and the second chapter began: AI agents that respond across chat, email, and voice at the quality of the best human teams.
We're 100 people, profitable, and have raised €18M in funding (last round 4.5 years ago, we've been growing on our own money since). Headquartered in Berlin.

In this role you own all of finance at Superchat end to end and report directly to the founders. When the board or our investors have a question about the numbers, you're the one who answers it.You'll take over our financial model and turn it into something the whole company can steer by. You'll own accounting through to the P&L, run forecasting and liquidity planning, and lead the annual audit.
7+ years of finance experience.You know the full cycle first-hand, from closing to forecast to board reporting.

Closing and audit expertise.You independently own monthly and annual closings under HGB, including revenue recognition and accruals, and you coordinate the annual audit with our external auditors through to completed financial statements.
Expert financial modelling.You build driver-based, integrated three-statement models from scratch and you document them so that others can operate them too.

Forecasting.You've owned full budget and forecast cycles, you bring together top-down targets and bottom-up input from team leads, and you treat forecast accuracy as a measurable figure that has to improve.
Business partner.You deliver a reasoned recommendation, not just the numbers and you follow up on whether it gets implemented.

Experience with investors and the board.You've prepared and presented board materials, and you've been through a financial due diligence - ideally on the company side.Bridges finance and startup culture. You bring the rigour a finance function demands, while working productively with fast decisions and shifting priorities.
Appetite for automation.You actively look for ways to take manual work out of the close and the reporting cycle, so the team's time goes into analysis rather than assembly.

Strong communicator.You translate complex financial data into clear narratives for stakeholders without a finance background, and you're confident in the room with founders, board and investors. Fluent German and English, written and verbal.
Manages the status quo.You run an inherited function competently, but you don't develop it further.
Reports instead of advising.You deliver numbers without drawing a recommendation from them, and consider the job done once the report is sent.
Treats the model as personal property.You build something only you can operate with undocumented logic and manual overrides nobody else can follow. Uncomfortable in front of investors.
Looking for predictability.You need stable priorities and permanently fixed responsibilities.

You’ll sit in our Accounting Integrations team and help ensure spend data (expenses, receipts, VAT, categories) flows cleanly from Pleo into the accounting systems and ERPs finance teams rely on, with minimal manual work. European accounting and ERP systems, and/or an accounting qualification.Partner negotiation experience and/or additional European languages.Working knowledge of APIs, data mapping or implementation projects.Why this role is a good fit for youThis role is a good fit for you if:You enjoy bringing real accounting expertise into product decisions and can explain complex finance concepts in a clear, practical way.You like owning problems end to end - from identifying the right solution to working with others to ship it.You’re motivated by improving workflows for finance teams and can connect day-to-day pain points to measurable outcomes.This role is not a good fit for you if:You want a role where you control delivery directly, rather than delivering through internal teams and external partners.You prefer depth in a single system over context switching across many tools, markets and accounting practices.You’re looking for a purely accounting or purely technical role, without the column3: Indépendant | Rémunération à la commission uniquement | Territoire de vente local | Commissions déplafonnées&lt
Nous recherchons des commerciaux terrain expérimentés, à l’aise pour se rendre dans une entreprise, engager la conversation avec le propriétaire et convaincre de nouveaux commerçants.&lt

En tant que conseiller commercial itinérant indépendant, vous vendrez les solutions de paiement, de point de vente et logicielles de SumUp aux petites et moyennes entreprises de votre région. Vous identifierez vous-même vos prospects, gérerez votre portefeuille d’opportunités et accompagnerez les clients lors de leur mise en route.&lt

Vous devrez justifier d’une expérience en prospection à froid et apprécier la vente en face à face sur le terrain. Vous gérerez votre propre activité et organiserez vos démarches commerciales de manière autonome, tout en bénéficiant de la formation et du soutien de SumUp.&lt
Trouver de nouveaux clients grâce à des visites en face à face, de la prospection en porte-à-porte et des démarches directes.&lt
Cibler les entreprises locales générant d’importants volumes de paiement et susceptibles de tirer parti des produits SumUp.&lt
Poser des questions sur le fonctionnement de chaque entreprise et recommander des solutions adaptées en matière de paiement, de matériel, de caisse et de logiciels.&lt
Gérer le processus de vente depuis le premier échange, en passant par les démonstrations de produits, la gestion des objections et la conclusion, dans le cadre du partenariat.&lt
Aider les clients à mettre en place et à commencer à utiliser leurs produits SumUp.&lt
Établir des relations avec les chefs d’entreprise et demander des recommandations aux clients satisfaits.&lt
Planifier vos visites et vos suivis afin d’optimiser votre temps sur le terrain.&lt
Suivre votre activité, vos opportunités et vos résultats de vente, et transmettre les informations nécessaires au traitement des ventes.&lt
Échanger avec votre interlocuteur SumUp pour bénéficier de son expertise produit et de conseils commerciaux.&lt

Au moins un an d’expérience dans la vente sur le terrain dans des secteurs tels que les télécommunications, l’énergie, les technologies d’entreprise, la gestion des déchets, les systèmes de sécurité ou l’approvisionnement en produits alimentaires et boissons.&lt
Une expérience de la prospection à froid, notamment en démarchant des entreprises en face à face et en trouvant vos propres prospects.&lt
Une expérience de la vente auprès de petites et moyennes entreprises et des relations directes avec les propriétaires ou les décideurs.&lt

Des résultats démontrables en matière d’acquisition de nouveaux clients et d’atteinte d’objectifs commerciaux. Nous vous demanderons des exemples de vos réalisations et de la manière dont vous y êtes parvenu.&lt
La capacité à gérer un processus de vente de la première prise de contact à la conclusion, y compris la gestion des questions et des objections.&lt
Un bon sens de l’organisation et un suivi rigoureux.&lt
La capacité à gérer les refus, à tirer les leçons des retours d’expérience et à persévérer.&lt
Une bonne compréhension du statut d’indépendant et la volonté de développer votre portefeuille de clients.&lt
La capacité à vous déplacer sur votre territoire de vente afin de rencontrer régulièrement vos prospects et clients.&lt
Un réseau existant de chefs d’entreprise locaux susceptibles de bénéficier des produits SumUp.&lt
Une expérience dans le domaine des paiements, des services aux commerçants ou des systèmes de point de vente.&lt
Une expérience de la vente par téléphone est un atout, mais vous devez également avoir vendu en face à face sur le terrain.&lt

Il s’agit d’une activité indépendante, rémunérée exclusivement à la commission, sans salaire de base ni revenu minimum garanti. Les commissions sont déplafonnées et dépendent de vos résultats commerciaux et de l’activité des commerçants apportés.&lt
Le système de commissions comprend, dans le cadre des conditions Partner :&lt
Paiements : 50 % du revenu net annualisé lié aux transactions.&lt
Matériel : 50 % du prix de vente retenu dans le barème.&lt
Logiciels et abonnements : 50 % du montant annuel retenu dans le barème.&lt
Revenu résiduel : 20 % du revenu net mensuel généré par les commerçants apportés, pendant une durée maximale de trois ans.&lt
Avantage de bienvenue : trois fois le montant habituel des commissions résiduelles pendant les trois premiers mois.&lt
Primes supplémentaires liées à certains produits ou opérations commerciales.&lt
Les nouveaux partenaires bénéficient des conditions Partner pendant la période de lancement. Leur maintien est ensuite soumis aux critères d’activité du programme

column1: legal-ai-engineer-zurich-309794,Legartis,Legal AI Engineer (Zurich),Zurich,False,1791284954,"DescriptionLegartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does.Joining Legartis is not taking a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and lawyers, who do not chase hype
column2: we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place.Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published.Your missionMost companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first ""wow"" moment themselves. When they say ""that won't work for us"" or ""we'll build it ourselves"", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.Your profileThe person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not ""lawyer who is good with computers"". It is legal quant: a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why ""they did not understand the value"" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome.You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus.Why us?Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title.We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one.Real ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP).Build in public. We want you to keep publishing what you build, because it makes you better and it makes us visible.Offices in Berlin, Leipzig, and Zurich with a flexible hybrid setup. Regular apéros, lunches, and hiking trips as we enjoy the journey together.ProcessExpectations. A conversation with the People Manager about the role and who you are.Depth. Your mandate is the value discipline across the whole book: the Enterprise, Mid-Market, and Commercial accounts where no one is embedded, and where value today is quantified deal by deal or not at all. You will build the frameworks, benchmarks, calculators, and playbooks that let every seller articulate and measure value consistently, and you will use what you learn from strategic deployments to make that methodology sharper.This is not a quota-carrying role, nor is it a traditional advisory function. Use insights from existing deployments to help customers understand what they have achieved and identify where ElevenLabs can drive additional impact.Work directly with the data. Analyze customer and industry data, build models, pressure-test assumptions, and develop recommendations yourself. You should be equally comfortable working in the details and communicating the implications.Partner with Deployment. On strategic accounts, work alongside Deployment Strategists who own the account-level business case, contributing methodology and capturing what works into reusable assets. Across the rest of the book, be the primary owner of value quantification and measurement.Influence senior stakeholders. You can move quickly across industries, customer types, and use cases while maintaining a high bar for analytical rigor.Ability to operate globally. column2: DRJoin GlassDollar and help build the system some of Europe's largest companies use to find, test, and adopt startup technology.We're looking for an engineer who wants considerably more responsibility than ""implement what's in the ticket"". You'll take an ambiguous problem, shape it together with product, make the important technical decisions, ship it, and stay close enough to see whether it worked.We expect you to have opinions. We also expect you to be good enough to change them.The problem we're solvingLarge organisations are remarkably good at accumulating problems. A company with 100,000 employees can have thousands of operational challenges across its business units. Somewhere outside that organisation, a startup has probably already built part of the solution. Getting those two things to meet still happens through spreadsheets, long email threads, and meetings whose primary output is another meeting.GlassDollar OS is the operating system for venture clienting: problem → startup discovery → evaluation → PoC → adoption, in one repeatable workflow.Our customers are some of Europe's largest organisations, so the software has to move quickly and behave like something an enterprise can depend on. That tension creates the interesting engineering problems.What we're looking forYou can take a problem further than the ticket. Work often starts with something incomplete, like ""customers need a better way to manage X"". You'll shape the problem with product, challenge assumptions, and decide what belongs in this iteration. Strong opinions about what we build, not only how, are expected here.You care about product. You want to know who you're building for, why the problem matters, and what success looks like. That context should shape your technical decisions.You have technical judgement. There is rarely one correct architecture. You know when the boring solution beats the ambitious one, when an abstraction helps and when it hides the problem, and when a small feature is about to create six months of technical debt. We expect you to reason about API boundaries, data models, permissions, performance, failure modes, testing, observability, and rollout, and to raise concerns with a clear argument attached.You make the system better, not just the feature. column1: full-stack-product-developer-berlin-440978,Tablemedia,Full Stack Product Developer (m/w/d),Berlin,False,1791544161,"Aufgaben  Du willst Technologie gestalten, die direkt etwas bewegt? Bei Table.Briefings entwickeln wir digitale Produkte für ein wachsendes Medienunternehmen. column1: We are an engineering organization. Our mission is to “Ship great software” and build custom, large-scale software platforms on time, on budget, on target and on quality.&nbsp
In over two decades, we have never failed to deliver what we promised.&nbsp
85% of our members are software engineers with a background in computer science, physics or mathematics, many also with a strong background in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence.
freiheit.com technologies was founded in Hamburg in the midst of the first internet boom in the last millennium in 1999.
Since then, we’ve been building custom software platforms and helping our clients to create their future business models based on software.
For over a quarter of a century, we have been working for the ""Who's Who"" of German and European industry and business. Retail, automotive, e-commerce, healthcare and more.
Our large-scale software platforms are used by millions of users every day. Each product has a business-critical, strategic relevance for our clients.
We are a team of 300+ members with people from all over the world. In our engineering hubs in Hamburg and Lisbon we come together to create things that no one has built before.

Our teams work data-driven to constantly optimize their own productivity by removing friction from their work. Each member takes on end-to-end responsibility for their work. To be successful, you need to be productive. To be productive, you need to be efficient and effective.
Technology never rests. Neither do we.
Your responsibility: From day one, you’ll own your stories and take end-to-end responsibility for your tasks.&nbsp
Your team: You'll work in a small team of no more than five full-stack engineers. Like this, our teams are more efficient and can move fast.

Your work: You’ll be involved in the entire software engineering lifecycle of your project - from product requirements and design to testing, deployment and operations. You’ll see how people actually use what you build and continuously improve it based on user feedback and real usage data.

Your projects: We partner with clients across all industries who trust us with their most challenging software problems. We take full ownership from the first idea to the final roll-out. You’re not joining a client team as an extra pair of hands - you’re part of the team responsible for solving the problem. We don’t do body leasing.
Your impact: You will contribute to some of the largest, business-critical and most demanding software projects in Europe.

Your perspective: No matter your experience, everyone starts as a newbie and passes through all of our engineering levels. From owning small to medium feature sets to being responsible for the whole codebase. Here you can learn how to build and run large-scale software systems – and grow into a full-stack software engineer.&nbsp

Your community: You’ll work with smart, like-minded people who care about what they do and the people around them. With over 300 people across our Hamburg and Lisbon hubs, we work hard, support each other, and make sure to create a work environment where you can become the best version of yourself.&nbsp

We are a company for engineers by engineers. Most of your time is spent solving problems with like-minded people, writing software and working together with your team in our beautiful offices in the heart of Hamburg &amp
We expect a lot. It's not easy. But we guarantee you it will be fun.
A degree: Bachelor's, Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Physics or a closely related field.&nbsp

Problem solving: We hire our members for their problem-solving abilities, not specific programming languages. We value strong engineering fundamentals, analytical thinking, and the ability to turn complex ideas into working code. We believe: if you know how to code, debug, and solve complex problems, you can learn any language. We hire smart engineers, not language specialists.
A genuine curiosity for programming: Whether through interesting pet projects, hackathons, competitive programming.
A habit of stepping outside your comfort zone: Whether through competitive tutoring, scholarships, or even competitive sports, anything else where you pushed yourself and grew from it.
Algorithms and data structures, understanding time &amp
Experience in Go, Kotlin, TypeScript or JavaScript
Experience in front end development, like ReactJS, Angular, Vue or Flutter/Dart
Functional programming with Common Lisp, Clojure or Haskell
Experience working with distributed systems in the Cloud
Experience in Machine Learning and Data Science&nbsp

From reviewing your CV to the final hire, its engineers who are in charge of the recruiting process. Your first interview will be conducted by one of our engineers. No recruiters, no script reading. You’ll talk directly with the engineers you’ll be building alongside, so we can dive straight into real technical problems and our ways of working.&nbsp
If you ask anyone why they work here, it's pretty likely that they will say “because of the people” and “because I've never learned so much in my life”.
We believe that productive people are happy people.&nbsp
In our engineering hubs in Hamburg and Lisbon, you will meet people from all over the world.&nbsp
Here you have the opportunity to work with intelligent people on interesting tasks and complete projects from idea to operations – end-to-end.

Becoming a well-rounded professional in your field of expertise is a long journey that takes many years of hard work and learning. Being a member of our company will ask a lot of you and no one can do the work for you.
Our company is a place where you can become the best version of yourself.&nbsp

column1: legal-ai-engineer-berlin-or-leipzig-295650,Legartis,Legal AI Engineer (Berlin or Leipzig),Berlin,False,1791522555,"DescriptionLegartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. column2: we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place.Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published.Your missionMost companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first ""wow"" moment themselves. When they say ""that won't work for us"" or ""we'll build it ourselves"", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.Your profileThe person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not ""lawyer who is good with computers"". It is legal quant: a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why ""they did not understand the value"" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome.You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus.Why us?Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title.We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one.Real ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP).Build in public. We want you to keep publishing what you build, because it makes you better and it makes us visible.Offices in Berlin, Leipzig, and Zurich with a flexible hybrid setup. Regular apéros, lunches, and hiking trips as we enjoy the journey together.ProcessExpectations. A conversation with the People Manager about the role and who you are.Depth. project-planner-data-centres-buildings-high-tech-infrastructure-frankfurt-berlin-munich-hybrid-291591,Laminarprojects,Project Planner (Data Centres/Buildings/High-tech/Infrastructure) -  Frankfurt/Berlin/Munich (Hybrid),Frankfurt,False,1791522245,"Are you a bit tired of the standard, old-fashioned way of doing things in the construction industry?&nbsp

Have you always cared about the importance of proper planning and the connection between the schedule and the real, day-to-day delivery of the job?&nbsp
Have you ever wanted to work a bit more flexibly but still be hands-on in construction and improving the industry?&nbsp
Sounds like a dream. Well, it isn’t. It’s quite real! Read on.&nbsp

If you’ve already heard about us, you’re probably reading this because you’re tired of the typical, chaotic ways of doing things in construction. But in case you haven’t, we’re a high-end project management consultancy and tech developer with a focus on upgrading the way construction projects are delivered.
Improving construction strengthens the very foundation of human civilisation. (Check out our short film about it.)

We bring transparency and control to projects through a pragmatic mix of the latest tech, our own processes, and a big dose of common sense. We then take our deep understanding of these projects and we invest heavily into developing the digital solutions that anyone can use to deliver their projects better. (Check out Shape, our construction management tech, to see what we’re doing.)

The core of all this is our true secret sauce: our people. We only recruit the very best, both in capability and personality. We’re deeply focused on designing a new type of organisation that’s optimised for the flourishing of the people in the team first and foremost. People who join us develop fast as a whole person in ways they never imagined. (Read more about our vision and missions.)

This approach has allowed us to grow from just two people in 2017 to over 220 today. We have a stable, repeat client base across infrastructure and complex building projects in the UK and internationally, and we’re still growing fast. Joining us isn’t just some “job”. It’s a transformative educational experience. We challenge you to be your best self in all aspects of life. There are many diverse and interesting challenges available. It’s up to you to guide yourself into whichever areas you’re most interested – we’ll enable it.&nbsp
(Get to know us better by watching a few more of our videos.)
Core values for a good life
A life of human flourishing is all about meaningful relationships and challenging yourself to create a positive impact, so our values reflect the four levels of relationships that each of us has:
- Grow yourself – your relationship with yourself&nbsp
- Care about people – your relationship with others around you&nbsp
- Execute to greatness – your relationship with your team&nbsp
- Build civilisation – your relationship with humanity and the world&nbsp
We enshrined our values in our vision:
We exist so that everyone in our team can flourish in a high-impact community that:
- Inspires us to develop ourselves to become better humans&nbsp
- Empowers us to pursue our own learning adventures&nbsp
By first doing this, we can achieve the highest levels of value for the world.
And enable the achievement of our vision through our two missions:
- To fully digitalise the construction of human civilisation&nbsp
- To create a new type of organisation that enables human flourishing while delivering a huge positive impact on society&nbsp

You’ll be enhancing the delivery of the most complex and interesting projects in the world through the power of project planning to the very highest standards. You’ll devise strategies and tactics to improve the way the project is delivered. You’ll translate this knowledge into a logic-linked plan and analyse it using planning software. Then you’ll use the plan to help the teams understand what to prioritise.&nbsp
This role is part of our Project Management Consultancy team which focuses on:
- Understanding what the real problems of projects are&nbsp
- Implementing the best solutions to those problems&nbsp
- Developing scalable best practices, tools and technology&nbsp

More specifically, you’ll be part of our Project Planning Team, who are industry leaders in the planning of complex construction projects. Your initial leader will be one of our planning discipline directors.
1. To make construction projects deliver to near perfection&nbsp
2. To create scalable and repeatable solutions to common problems&nbsp
3. To develop yourself and everyone around you&nbsp
1. Own the plan: Own the project plan for one or more projects and ensure that the project is working to it effectively. Ensure delays are mitigated and managed commercially&nbsp

3. Report and inform: Provide simple, actionable reports to stakeholders at all levels that help them deliver their part of the project more efficiently and effectively&nbsp

5. Develop everyone: Maximise the development of your team personally and professionally and educate our clients to improve as well&nbsp

- You prefer to do your own thing rather than work with a team

It’s common for people to be exposed to several projects in their first year with us. You’ll work on some of the most complex and interesting environments in the world. Salesforce and connected systems.You make evidence-based decisions to prioritize your backlog, focusing relentlessly on business growth and operational scalability.You partner closely with Salesforce actively guiding internal teams through training, change management and process adoption.You track clear success metrics to measure operational efficiency gains, while exploring AI applications to column1: platform-engineer-munchen-419801,Ecoplanet Green Operations Gmbh,Platform Engineer (m/f/d),München,False,1791511778,"What we are buildingecoplanet builds the operating system for the energy transition. Our software helps European businesses cut energy costs, run more efficiently, and take the pain out of managing energy day to day. We are around 40 people and backed by EQT Ventures, HV Capital and others.Why This Role MattersYou build and run the platform the whole product sits on: the event streams, the backend services and the cloud infrastructure everything else is built on. Meter readings arrive from industrial sites across Europe, through messages or us accessing APIs. Your job is to make sure that traffic lands reliably, moves through the system in a shape other teams can build on, and keeps doing so as the number of sites grows.You join a team of 12 engineers in two squads. Small team, real ownership, and what you build reaches customers in weeks rather than quarters.What you will work onEvent streaming. Kafka is the spine of the system. You own topic and schema design, partitioning, retention and delivery semantics  and the everyday reality behind them: consumers falling behind, replays, backfills, late and duplicated readings.Backend services in TypeScript. The ingestion services, integrations and APIs around that stream. Every site is a little different, so a good part of the job is turning that variety into one consistent interface the product squads can rely on.Cloud infrastructure on GCP. Compute, networking, IAM, infrastructure as code, CI/CD and observability. The goal is a paved road: other engineers ship and debug their own services without going through you.Technical direction. Where we invest in the platform, what we standardise, what we deliberately leave rough for now  and bringing the rest of the team along with it.What Sets You Up for SuccessMust have:At least 6–8 years building and running backend systems in production, including real time in a platform or infrastructure role that other engineers depended onStrong backend engineering in TypeScript. You have designed, shipped and operated services and APIs in it — not just touched it around the edges of a frontendHands-on with Kafka in production. Topic design, consumer groups, ordering and delivery guarantees, and what you actually do at 3am when a consumer group is hours behind. A comparable streaming platform is fine if you know it at that depthSolid on GCP or an equivalent cloud: containers, networking and IAM basics, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, monitoring and alerting. You have owned infrastructure, not just deployed onto itComfortable with high-volume time-series data: ingestion, data quality, backfills, and the everyday reality of late, missing and duplicated readingsYou have seen a few things. column1: customer-success-engineer-germany-80446,Vclusterlabs,Customer Success Engineer,Germany,False,1791481207,"As a Customer Success Engineer at vCluster, you aren't just managing accounts — you are the primary architect of customer outcomes after the deal closes. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. We know things can change in life and we’re happy to adjust the work environment for you along the way.Culture &amp

platform-engineer-gn-at-ai-efficiency-venture-berlin-76033,atlantic.vc,"Platform Engineer (gn) @ AI Efficiency Venture, Berlin","Berlin, Berlin, Germany",False,1791480641,"This is an Atlantic portfolio venture.About the VentureAI models have moved faster than most companies’ ability to put them to work. The capabilities are there
column2: knowing how to combine them effectively is still catching up.Frontier labs naturally put their own models first. Companies often follow suit, asking one general-purpose model to handle ten very different jobs. We believe there is far more to unlock in the models that already exist, even before the next generation arrives. That is the opportunity we are building around.We bring closed providers and open-weight models together behind a single API. Our engine breaks requests into their component parts, routes each to the right model within a cost budget, fine-tunes on customer data and checks the result against agreed quality standards. With no proprietary model to promote, we can choose the right combination for the task.Lower costs matter because of what they make possible: giving a small team the freedom to build something that would previously have required a much larger one.Our founder brings considerable drive, a hands-on approach and a strong sense of urgency to building the company. Backed by Atlantic at pre-seed, we are growing the engineering team to bring the product into production, with people already waiting to use it.About the RoleAs one of our first platform engineers, you will build the foundations that every product feature depends on: the gateway and router, usage and billing systems, customer key management and the European infrastructure underneath.Much of that platform is still taking shape. Working directly with the founder, CTO and founding AI engineer, you will help turn early architectural decisions into systems that remain reliable as the product grows.You will take capabilities from design through to production, thinking through their APIs, failure modes, deployment, observability and ongoing operation. In a team this small, building and running the system belong together. You will also work alongside our founding AI engineer on evals, embeddings and open-weight model serving, bringing platform engineering depth to the ML side of the product.Agentic engineering is central to how we work. You will use and help develop the harnesses and workflows that allow a small team to ship quickly, applying the coding fundamentals and judgement needed to stand behind what reaches production.There is a lot to build and an ambitious timeline ahead. We work with intensity, move quickly from decisions to execution and value people who take initiative and see things through.What You’ll Work OnYour first area of ownership will depend on your strengths and our priorities. From there, you will contribute across the platform as it develops.Gateway and routing: build a consistent API across model providers, with reliable streaming, fallbacks and safe handling of retries and provider errors.Cost optimisation: develop caching, history compression and model selection, measuring savings while keeping estimated costs distinct from actual spend.Usage and billing: build accurate accounting for model calls, usage reports, plan entitlements and invoice reconciliation.Agent infrastructure and integrations: support tool calls, cost limits, human approvals and runs that can recover safely from interruptions, alongside connectors for services such as Gmail, Slack and calendars.Tenancy and secrets: maintain workspace isolation, secure authentication and encrypted customer key management.European infrastructure and model serving: build and operate our cloud infrastructure, including the GPU capacity used to serve open-weight models.Production reliability: make systems observable, migrations reversible and releases safe, with tests that protect data integrity and logs that keep customer content and secrets private.The platform will evolve quickly. You will need to move comfortably between improving what exists and learning enough about a new problem to build the next piece well.Our StackOur backend is built in Python, with a TypeScript frontend in a shared monorepo.Backend: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic and LiteLLM.Data and queues: Postgres with row-level security and pgvector, Redis and arq.Frontend: Next.js, React and TypeScript.Cloud and infrastructure: Scaleway, Terraform and Kubernetes for GPU workloads.Auth and secrets: Zitadel, Secret Manager and KMS.Observability and testing: OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, Sentry, pytest and testcontainers, alongside frontend testing tools.You should be comfortable with the core backend technologies and ready to learn the rest as the work requires.About YouYou enjoy the craft of engineering and the responsibility of seeing your work used in production. Faced with an unclear problem, you can identify what matters, make sensible trade-offs and carry a solution through to release without someone planning every step.We are looking for:Experience building and operating production systems: several years of backend engineering with real users, typically three to six, and meaningful ownership of what you shipped.Strong Python fundamentals: confidence with async code, typing and testing. TypeScript experience is a plus.Platform engineering depth: practical experience with Postgres, Redis, queues, networking and Terraform. Kubernetes experience is useful, particularly for our GPU infrastructure.Sound engineering judgement: clear APIs, tenant isolation, data integrity, partial failure and safe rollouts. You can explain both your decisions and what you chose to leave out.A working understanding of ML systems: familiarity with LLMs, embeddings, evals, model serving and fine-tuning. Experience with LLM APIs, streaming and token costs is a strong plus.Practical agentic engineering experience: you use coding agents effectively and can develop and evaluate their workflows, while independently understanding, reviewing and debugging the code they produce.A disciplined approach to measurement: you benchmark changes, question assumptions and use evidence to understand whether an improvement holds up.Initiative and drive: you enjoy getting deep into a problem, finding a way forward and putting in the work to make it happen.This is an experienced individual-contributor role, with ownership of the capabilities you build and close collaboration across the founding team.Fluent English is required

column1: chief-technology-officer-all-identities-berlin-hybrid-307588,Goreha,Chief Technology Officer (all identities),Berlin (hybrid),False,1791480584,"What to ExpectCaspar Health is entering its next growth phase. Our digital care is becoming increasingly critical to clinic and hospital operations. At the same time, we are progressing towards medical-device obligations and expanding AI-enabled ways of working.As CTO, you will own Technology and Engineering at C-level. You will report to the CEO, lead Engineering with full functional and disciplinary responsibility and work as a peer to the CPO.Your job is not to become the bottleneck or Caspar's most important individual technologist. You will build a strong leadership layer and an Engineering system that moves quickly with security, resilience and evidence. You will stay close enough to technology to judge important decisions, risks and AI-enabled development through current practice.This position is based in Germany and must be performed, living in Germany. Due to our current payroll and social security arrangements, we cannot offer permanent employment from abroad. Applicants must therefore be able to perform their duties from Germany starting on their first day of work and must already have the necessary authorization to work in Germany.Your ChallengesTranslate company and product strategy into a technology strategy with clear capabilities, investments, risks and measurable 18-month proof points.Lead all Engineering teams and Engineering leads, including Platform, Infrastructure, DevOps/SRE, developer experience and Engineering-owned quality automation.Build a strong leadership layer, clear domain ownership, distributed knowledge and resilient internal and external capacity without single-person dependencies.Own architecture, technology choices, reliability, security implementation, technical evidence and reporting, and regulated development for critical clinic and hospital workflows. Keep Caspar ready for deep technical scrutiny with current architecture and ownership evidence, demonstrable Caspar IP ownership, auditable security and compliance evidence, a credible AI story and no critical single-person dependencies.Own the incident system and lead major or trust-critical escalations. You are not the standing first-line on-call engineer. Ensure postmortem actions are completed and verified.Plan the Engineering budget and capacity. Decide within the approved envelope on technology, vendors and build, buy or outsource options, including lifecycle cost and continuity.Shape AI-enabled Engineering through current personal practice. Create measurable leverage without weakening security, maintainability, review quality, traceability or regulated assurance.Make credible commitments with Product. Product owns outcomes and scope intent. You own technical feasibility, capacity and release readiness, and stop unsupported or unsafe commitments.Involve Medical, Quality, Information Security, Privacy and Legal early. Engineering turns requirements into reusable controls, tests and evidence. Independent functions retain review, stop and risk-acceptance rights.Establish clear data contracts with Data. Technology owns production and operational data systems. Data owns semantics, certified analytical datasets, metric governance, analytical quality, experimentation and decision science.Represent Caspar in high-stakes technical discussions with clinics, hospital IT, integration partners, auditors, investors and the board.What success looks likeIn your first year, you will:Build a strong Engineering leadership layer and accountable ownership for critical systemsConnect technology choices and investment to company strategy and reviewable proof points, then complete a deep external technical review at customer, auditor or investor standard with no unresolved material findingsImprove delivery predictability, release quality, resilience and regulated evidenceMake cooperation between Engineering, Infrastructure and independent Security durable and effectiveCreate measurable impact through AI-enabled Engineering without weakening security or qualityYour ProfileYou have managed multiple Engineering leaders and led a multi-team organization through a meaningful scale or rigor transition.You have owned technology strategy, budget, capacity and build, buy or outsource decisions at executive level, with evidence of their impact.You have led Engineering in regulated, security-critical or high-availability systems. Medical-device or digital-health experience is a plus, not a prerequisite.You have built and scaled cloud-SaaS products, ideally in a regulated environment. Health-tech or medical-device experience is a plus, not a prerequisite. You also bring broad systems depth across backend services, web and mobile clients, APIs and integrations, data flows, observability, security and operations. Our exact stack is not a hard filter.You currently work hands-on with agentic development workflows and can show how you used, constrained or rejected AI output and made it scaleYou have shipped products that achieved meaningful customer and business outcomes and bring product judgement and pace, not only engineering rigor. You can challenge Product constructively, make business and technical trade-offs explicit and protect credible commitments under pressure.You build trust with teams, customers, partners, auditors, investors and boards without acting as a rescuer or creating dependence on yourself.You are business-fluent in German and English.A university degree or fixed number of years is not required. We care about demonstrated impact, judgement and responsibility you have personally carried.Why Caspar Health?A genuine C-level mandate with ownership of Engineering and company technology strategy.The opportunity to combine speed and rigor for digital clinical workflows and make a tangible difference to care.A clear Product-Technology peer model with shared decisions instead of hidden hand-offs.Remote-first within Germany with flexible working hours. Regular in-person leadership in Berlin is part of the role. There is no fixed weekly office quota. By combining autonomous platforms with intelligent software and AI, Quantum Systems enables customers to operate, understand and act across domains.Join Quantum-Systems and help bring autonomous ground systems into real world operations. As Senior E/E Engineer EMC and Compliance, you will own electromagnetic compatibility across our UGV platforms, starting with our Mandrill UGV: from the grounding and shielding concept on the drawing board to the certificate that puts our vehicles on public roads and into military service. Your goal is one robust E/E design baseline that passes civil homologation (UN ECE R10) and military qualification (MIL-STD-461, AECTP 500) without costly redesign loops. This is a senior engineer role with real ownership and room to grow. You build our EMC capability from the ground up, set the strategy, decide early in the design, and lead campaigns through to certification. You will work at the intersection of high power electronics, vehicle E/E, radios and mission payloads, autonomy compute, suppliers, test houses and authorities. As the platform family and team grow, this role can develop into leading our EMC and compliance function. What is your Day to Day Mission:EMC Strategy and Compliance OwnershipDefine and own the EMC and E3 compliance strategy for our UGV platforms, covering civil vehicle approval (UN ECE R10, E mark for vehicle and ESA) and military qualification (MIL-STD-461G, MIL-STD-464, AECTP 500 / AECTP 250, MIL-STD-1275).Translate customer, NATO and national requirements into an EMC control plan, requirement matrix and test strategy, and keep them current as configurations evolve.Act as the technical interface to accredited test houses, technical services, type approval authorities and defence customers during qualification and acceptance.EMC by DesignDevelop and integrate the grounding, bonding, shielding and harness concept for the complete vehicle, with special focus on high voltage and high power electronics: traction inverters, DC/DC converters, battery systems and chargers together with outstanding team of engineersRun EMC design reviews for schematics, PCBs, harnesses, enclosures and connectors
column2: specify filters, transient protection and shielding concepts.Manage RF coexistence on a dense platform:  datalinks, GNSS, tactical radios and payload emitters working side by side without degrading each other.Flow down EMC requirements to suppliers, run component level reviews and assess their test evidence.Test, Troubleshooting and QualificationBuild our in house pre compliance lab (LISN, spectrum analyser, near field probes, current clamps, automated measurement scripts) so issues are found on the bench, not in the chamber.Plan, witness and lead full compliance campaigns at component, subsystem and vehicle level
column3: drive root cause analysis and verified fixes when tests fail.Use simulation (e.g. FEKO, CST, LTspice) where it saves test iterations.Cross Functional Collaboration and StandardsWork closely with payload integration, vehicle E/E, mechanical, autonomy and manufacturing teams so EMC is built in, not bolted on.Create EMC control plans, test procedures, reports and qualification evidence, and turn lessons learned into internal EMC design rules for every future platform and payload.What you bring to the team:Degree in Electrical Engineering, Information Technology, Electronics or a comparable technical field.8+ years of EMC experience in automotive, commercial vehicle, rail, aerospace or defence, including ownership of at least one product through formal qualification or type approval.Deep knowledge of automotive EMC (e.g. UN ECE R10, CISPR 25, ISO 11452, ISO 7637, ISO 10605) and working knowledge of military EMC (MIL-STD-461
column4: ideally MIL-STD-464, AECTP 500, DEF STAN 59-411 or VG 95370/95373). Strong automotive profiles willing to extend into the military world are very welcome.Solid experience with EMC of high voltage and power electronics systems.Practical measurement expertise at component and vehicle level, and the ability to set up and automate test systems (e.g. Python, Matlab).Structured root cause analysis, ideally backed by methods such as Six Sigma, and audit ready documentation.Confident communication with engineers, suppliers, test labs, authorities and military customers.Fluent in German and English.High ownership, focus on teamwork, pragmatic, and happy to work directly on vehicles and in the workshop.Your Benefits: Direct impact: See your contributions rapidly integrated from cutting-edge research into industrialized products, flying in the field within short development cycles. Culture &amp

enterprise-solutions-architect-gn-bremen-128147,Workidentity,Enterprise Solutions Architect (gn),Bremen,False,1791479408,"EinleitungEnterprise Solution Architect (gn)Schwerpunkt EAM-Plattform und GovernanceWie oft im Leben bekommt man die Chance, Enterprise Architecture nicht zu reparieren, sondern von null aufzubauen? Die meisten EAM-Rollen beginnen mit einem Erbe: ein Tool, das vor Jahren jemand anderes gekauft hat, ein Repository mit Stand von vorgestern, eine Community, die sich aus Pflicht trifft. Diese Rolle beginnt mit einem leeren Blatt.Unser Mandant, ein international tätiger Dienstleistungskonzern mit mehreren tausend Mitarbeitenden, stellt seine IT gerade organisatorisch neu auf. Die Holding, die alle Geschäftsbereiche steuert, baut dabei Enterprise Architecture Management als eigenständige Funktion auf, mit eigenem Tooling, eigenen Prozessen und konzernweiter Geltung. Tool-Auswahl, Metamodell, Governance: nichts davon ist entschieden. Das wird deine Entscheidung. Solche Konstellationen gibt es selten und sie halten nicht lange. In zwei Jahren ist die neue IT-Organisation gesetzt, und wer dann kommt, arbeitet in Strukturen, die jemand anderes gebaut hat. Jetzt ist der Moment, in dem man sie baut.Worum es geht Enterprise Architecture scheitert selten an fehlenden Frameworks. Sie scheitert daran, dass niemand das Repository pflegt, das Tool nicht mit den Quellsystemen spricht und die Architektur-Community nach dem dritten Meeting einschläft. Diese Rolle verhindert genau das. Du baust die Grundlage, auf der EAM in diesem Konzern funktioniert. Prozesse, die Menschen tatsächlich befolgen. Eine Plattform, die ihre Daten automatisiert bezieht, statt dass jemand sie abtippt.Deine AufgabenDu definierst, wie Architekturarbeit im Konzern abläuft: Prozessmodelle, Rollen und Verantwortlichkeiten, Beschreibungen und Anforderungskataloge.Du wählst das EAM-Tool aus, von der Marktsondierung über die Ausschreibung bis zur Entscheidung, und verantwortest danach Implementierung und Konfiguration.Du konzipierst die Anbindung an Konfigurationsdatenbank, Service-Management und Cloud-Umgebungen, damit das Repository aktuell bleibt, ohne dass jemand es manuell nachführt.Du entwickelst das Architektur-Metamodell weiter, wenn Geschäft oder Technologie es verlangen und misst die Reife der Prozesse regelmäßig gegen Industriestandards.Du probierst neue Methoden aus, etwa Capability Maps oder Wertstromanalysen, und entscheidest, was davon in diesen Konzern passt.Du sorgst für Betrieb und Skalierbarkeit der Plattform, inklusive Rollen und Zugriffskonzepten und definierst Kennzahlen für Datenqualität.Du entwirfst Schulungs- und Onboarding-Formate, pflegst die Dokumentation und schreibst die Leitfäden, die neue Nutzende wirklich lesen.Dein ProfilMehrjährige Erfahrung in Solution- oder Enterprise-Architektur, gern mit technischer Leitungsverantwortung für eine gewachsene IT-Landschaft.Praxis in Einführung und Administration eines marktgängigen EAM-Tools, etwa Ardoq, LeanIX, Sparx EA oder vergleichbar.Sichere Anwendung gängiger Architektur-Frameworks wie TOGAF oder ArchiMate, idealerweise zertifiziert.Erfahrung mit Architektur-Boards oder Communities, und ein Gespür dafür, wie man sie am Leben hält.Abgeschlossenes Studium in Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse.BenefitsUnbefristete Festanstellung in Vollzeit in einer Konzernholding mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen.
